title: Admin activity write-once ledger with residency-anchored retention
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a write-once, tamper-evident ledger for admin-level actions (role changes, privileged access grants, config flips) that is residency-aware and can be exported as cryptographically verifiable evidence. The ledger should satisfy regional data residency constraints, support retention policies per-customer and per-region, and provide automated export bundles for compliance teams and auditors. This ticket implements the core storage & export orchestration plus a lightweight audit API for Console and Dedicated/private deploys.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger append-only semantics enforced: once a record is committed it cannot be mutated or deleted via API
Records include cryptographic hash chain metadata to allow offline tamper detection
Retention settings can be scoped by customer and by region, with enforcement at write-time and periodic enforcement job
Export bundles can be generated on-demand and on-schedule in WORM-compatible format and delivered to S3/GCP buckets with signed manifests
Console shows per-customer retention policy and last-export timestamps; export operation is auditable
Integration tests cover failover of storage backends (multi-region) and proof verification flow
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha: Kickoff — scoped MVP for admin actions only (no user-level access logs) to reduce surface area. Decided to reuse existing event schema with added ledger envelope metadata.
2025-02-13 Marco: Prototype of append path complete. Using a two-step commit (write metadata + commit marker) to preserve durability semantics across S3-like and block-store backends.

2025-02-15 Security review (Samantha Chen): Requested inclusion of a per-record HMAC and optional public key signature for enterprise customers wanting third-party verification — added to scope as opt-in.

2025-02-17 PM feedback (Diego Ramos): Ensure export bundles support time-window filtering, signed manifest and checksum index. Add retention override audit trail when support staff applies temporary retention hold.

2025-02-20 Marco: Integration with residency policy engine prototype wired; write attempts that would violate residency are rejected with explicit error code. Added unit tests for region mismatch handling.
2025-02-21 Aisha: Raised follow-up to evaluate long-term storage cost for region-duplicated evidence and discuss tiered retention (hot 90d vs cold 7y) with finance for Dedicated customers.
changes: Add ledger envelope metadata to event model: sequence_id, prev_hash, signature, storage_region
New append-only storage service with S3/GCS/OnPrem adapters and commit marker
Residency check before commit using policy engine (reject or route)
Retention enforcement worker that marks eligible blobs for cold-archive or deletion marker (deletion marker only for non-WORM scopes)
Export orchestration service that composes signed bundle + manifest and writes to customer-specified bucket with optional SSE-KMS metadata
implementation_notes: We will keep the ledger records small (prefer structured JSON with compact fields) and store full verbose event payloads in separate object store when necessary to reduce ledger bloat

For WORM semantics on object stores without native immutability, we will enforce append-only via service-layer checks and maintain hash-chain proofs; for customers requiring cryptographic non-repudiation we will support periodic notarization to a ledger anchoring service (out of scope for MVP)
Export bundles must include a verification tool (small binary or script) that can validate the manifest and per-record hashes offline
Performance: expected median write latency increase ~8–12ms for ledger envelope generation and signing; benchmarked on prototype under 500rps
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Storage cost for long-term retention in multiple regions. Mitigation: support tiered storage lifecycle rules and configurable cross-region replication only when required by policy
Risk: Enforcement gaps between write-time checks and periodic retention worker. Mitigation: build an end-to-end test harness that simulates policy changes and verifies worker convergence within SLA
Risk: Customer distrust if export verification is non-trivial. Mitigation: provide signed manifests, simple verifier CLI, and optional use of customer-provided public keys
